Research supports order-breaking controls: shuffling sometimes barely changes sequential-recommender performance, suggesting accuracy alone cannot establish learned temporal structure ([dataset analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008)). Proposed training-only probes: for a bilinear transition score, decompose W into symmetric S=(W+Wᵀ)/2 and antisymmetric A=(W−Wᵀ)/2. Report actual score magnitudes |eᵢᵀAeⱼ| relative to symmetric and total contributions; parameter norms alone are insufficient. Measure forward-minus-reverse transition scores, excluding item biases, and compare against training transition-count asymmetry. A large antisymmetric component demonstrates directional capacity, not useful learning.

Use fixed training-prefix/next-item probes with identical candidate sets. Compare genuine transitions against reversed pairs and frequency-matched nontransitions; stratify results by source/target training frequency and transition support. Popularity matching helps prevent head-item preference from masquerading as directionality. Perturb histories by shuffling earlier items while preserving the last item, swapping the last two items, dropping recent items, and replacing the last item with a frequency- and similarity-matched alternative. Track score-margin changes and recommendation overlap against popularity-only, last-item similarity, and first-order transition baselines. These are proposed diagnostic controls, not established causal tests: perturbations can produce implausible histories, and first-order transitions need not imply higher-order reasoning ([pairwise sequence probes](https://www.research.atspotify.com/publications/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-really-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling)).

Select models exclusively using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, retaining its fixed users, negatives, and seed. Keep training probes descriptive. Separately report unseen-item full-catalog coverage, recommendation popularity, concentration, and recent-history similarity for the twenty training users; these do not establish relevance or simulator traits. Sampled and full-catalog metrics can rank models differently, so never interpret one as the other ([sampled-metric analysis](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651)).
